$comment: Bauhaus motion data: mechanical, precise, geometric. Springs are critically damped (damping ratio = c / (2 * sqrt(k * m)) of about 1.0), so nothing overshoots; the build simulates them into CSS linear() easings. Timings are rules of thumb, not read from historical film. Reference for the spirit: Moholy-Nagy's Light Prop for an Electric Stage (1930) and Ludwig Hirschfeld-Mack's coloured light plays (1922-23), built from circle, triangle and square in red, yellow and blue (research.md 2.2).
character: Mechanical and exact, like a well-made machine: parts slide along rails, turn by quarter turns and lock into place. Fast in, firm stop, no overshoot. Movement follows the grid and the piece's one diagonal.

springs.$comment: Critically damped presets. stiffness k, damping c, mass m. Approximate settle times from the build's simulation in brackets.

snap.use: Forms stamping into place, small UI feedback (about 360 ms).

machine.use: Default: bars, panels and text sliding along an axis (about 470 ms).

soft.use: Interactive UI transitions: hover, open, toggle. No overshoot (about 510 ms).

heavy.use: Large forms and full-width blocks entering (about 590 ms).

crisp.use: Timed moves: slides, wipes and quarter turns. Fast through the middle, firm at both ends.

linear.use: Continuous loops only: a rotating circle, a ticker, a bar travelling at constant speed.

step.use: Counting or cycling through a few states (like a mechanical counter or the banknote colour cycle).

exit.use: Things leaving: accelerate off along their axis.

draw.use: A bar or rule wipes on from one end along its own axis (scaleX from 0, or a stroke draw with pathLength="1").

pop.use: A form stamps in from scale 0 to 1, transform-origin at its centre or its grid corner. No overshoot.

rise.use: Text and blocks slide up into place on the baseline.

slide.use: A form or block travels along one axis (horizontal, vertical or the piece's diagonal) by whole grid modules.

turn.use: A square, triangle or quarter circle turns by exactly 90° (or 180°) about its centre or a corner, then stops.

rotate.use: A circle with a bar or cut across it turns once, continuously. The only free rotation, and only in loops.

cycle.use: The accent cycles through the combination's colours in hard steps (no cross-fade).

split.use: A colour block or bar opens the sheet by sliding apart along the diagonal or a grid line.

durations.$comment: Mechanical motion is quicker than organic motion. Rule of thumb for transforms that are not springs.
durations.formula: duration = 180 ms + 0.3 ms per pixel travelled (capped at 600 ms)

choreography.settleBeforeText: Each step starts when the previous one has locked in place: sequential, like an assembly line. Text starts after the last form stops.

loop.endsOn: The finished composition, all forms on the grid. A loop is a quarter turn, a slide out and back, or a colour cycle, never a wobble.

rules: Move along an axis: horizontal, vertical or the piece's one diagonal. Never along a curve, except a circle rotating about its own centre.
Rotations are in 90° steps, except a continuous loop on a circle.
Critically damped springs or crisp easing: no overshoot, no bounce, no wobble.
Slides travel whole grid modules and stop on the grid.
One thing moves at a time; the others are locked still.
Colour changes are hard cuts, never cross-fades.
With reduced motion: show the final composition. Loops, rotations and cycles stop.
